subject: HelioTech private GPU pool — initial sizing and topology questions
messages:
From: Asha Nair <asha@heliotech.com>
To: priyom@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff — HelioTech private pool sizing and network constraints

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for making time on Friday. As discussed, we want a compact private GPU pool (on-prem + VPC peering) to run a mixture of workloads: throughput-heavy embeddings, sporadic multi-turn chat inference, and nightly batch re-ranks. Our initial ask is: can Redwood provide sizing guidance and a proposed topology that meets a 95th-percentile tail latency of 150ms for chat (<= 512 tokens) and sustained throughput of 1000 embedding requests/sec, with predictable headroom for 2x burst for 10 minutes?

Constraints we need you to consider:
- Network egress is metered; we need to minimize cross-region traffic.
- Our on-prem NOC prefers a single east-coast PoP (NY) with a DR site in Chicago.
- We run a mix of fp16 and int8 models; some sessions keep KV caches warm for conversation continuity.

Attached: a short PDF with our traffic sample and a rough request/response size distribution (heliotech_sizing_questions.pdf). Can you propose an initial sizing and a topology sketch? Also include any assumptions about batching, cold-start warmup, and expected GPU types.

Asha
Lead SRE, HelioTech

P.S. Do you have a proposal template or matrix we should expect?
From: priyom@redwood.com (Priyom Das)
To: Asha Nair <asha@heliotech.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kickoff — HelioTech private pool sizing and network constraints

Hi Asha — thanks for the PDF and the sample traces. Quick confirmation: we can absolutely size around the two targets you called out (95p tail 150ms for chat, 1k embeddings/sec sustained) but need to validate a few assumptions before a firm number:

1) Embedding payload: are those single-text requests (~100 tokens avg) or batched client-side?
2) Chat mix: what percent of chat requests are short (<=128 tokens) vs long (256–512)?
3) KV cache retention: how many concurrent sessions will keep a warm cache for >5 minutes?

I'll put together an initial sizing matrix and a simple PoP/DR topology sketch (takes into account egress-metering). Expect a draft by Thu EOD.

Attached: initial sizing workbook (privpool_sizing_v1.xlsx) and a sketch placeholder (network_topology_draft.png).

Thanks — talk soon,
Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: marissa@redwood.com (Marissa Cole)
To: priyom@redwood.com, jonas@redwood.com, laura@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: HelioTech private pool — assumptions check for sizing

Looping you both in — Asha shared traffic samples and wants a sizing/topology for a mixed workload (embeddings + chat + nightly batch). I'm thinking we should approach with two candidate configs:

Candidate A — low-latency prioritized
- 8x A100-type GPUs (or equivalent Ampere 80GB) in NY PoP, dedicated to chat shards
- 4x A10/RTX 6000 for embeddings with batching (we expect steady 1k req/s)
- KV cache served on same nodes where possible; reserve 20% of GPU memory for KV to keep tail latency tight
- Network: single high-throughput crossconnect to HelioTech on-prem, mirrored to Chicago for DR (cold failover)
- Assumed batching: embeddings batched to 32 requests per batch, chat uses micro-batching with concurrency lanes

Candidate B — cost-balanced
- 6x H100-Q8 or 8x T4/RTX mix with more aggressive quantization for embeddings
- Autoscale headroom for 2x bursts via reserved burst-capacity pool (warm standby pods)
- Slightly higher tail latency target for chat (180–200ms) but much lower monthly cost

Questions for Jonas (runtime / routing):
- How realistic is 150ms 95p with 8x 80GB GPUs given micro-batching and KV locality?
- Do we need dedicated NICs or can we rely on host network with careful shaping?

Next step: Priyom to produce a matrix with QPS-to-GPU ratios, expected token/sec, and warmup timelines.

-Marissa
From: jonas@redwood.com (Jonas Weber)
To: marissa@redwood.com, priyom@redwood.com, laura@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelioTech private pool — assumptions check for sizing

Marissa — good split. Quick engineering reality-checks:

- 150ms 95p for 512-token chats is achievable only if KV cache hits are >= 85% and micro-batching is constrained to latencies <10ms on the queue. Otherwise tail spikes from cold KV lookups push 95p beyond 200ms. So we must size for cache residency (estimate concurrent warm sessions * cache size).
- For embeddings: 1k req/s sustained with batch=32 requires ~32 batches/sec throughput; on A10/T4 class GPUs we should expect ~28–40 batches/sec depending on model size and quant. Plan for 20–25% headroom for model variance.
- Network: dedicate an L2 crossconnect where possible. Host-network jitter on top of egress metering can ruin tail SLOs; a single-poP with DR is fine but add a static route to Chicago for warm standby if packet loss > 0.5%.

I'll sketch a QPS-to-GPU table and a simple admission policy (min free mem, min KV hit rate) by Thu morning. Also note: if HelioTech insists on single-PoP primary, reserve a small regional cache in Chicago to reduce cold-start penalties during failover.

-Jonas
Runtime Engineering Lead
From: priyom@redwood.com (Priyom Das)
To: Asha Nair <asha@heliotech.com>, HelioTech Eng Team <eng+infra@heliotech.com>
Cc: marissa@redwood.com, jonas@redwood.com, laura@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed sizing and topology — HelioTech private GPU pool (draft)

Asha / HelioTech team — attached is our draft sizing and topology based on your traces and the constraints you shared. TL;DR: two candidate configurations (low-latency and cost-balanced) with explicit assumptions and a QPS->GPU mapping. Highlights below, please read the assumptions section carefully.

Highlights (low-latency candidate):
- Primary PoP: NY colo — 8x 80GB GPUs (equivalent to A100-class); embeds handled on 4x A10/T4-class GPUs with batching=32.
- Performance expectation: 95p chat <= 150ms at steady-state when KV cache hit rate >= 85% and network jitter < 0.3%.
- Headroom: reserve 2 GPUs (standby warm pool) to absorb a 2x burst for up to 10 minutes; autoscale policy triggers additional pods if sustained beyond 10m.
- Networking: L2 crossconnect with dedicated NICs for inference traffic; mirrored passive link to Chicago for DR; egress shaping to limit cross-region replication during bursts.

Cost-balanced candidate notes:
- Reduce primary GPUs to 6x H100-Q8 (or 8x mixed smaller GPUs) with a slightly higher target 95p (180ms). Use more aggressive quantization (Q4/Q8) for embeddings.

Assumptions and risks:
- KV cache sizing matters more than raw GPU count; we included a cache-residency worksheet (see attached sheet). If warm sessions are higher than the sample (we assumed 8k concurrent warm sessions), tail latency will degrade quickly.
- Batch assumptions (embeddings batch size 32) critically affect effective throughput numbers — if clients send singletons, we'll need proportionally more embedding capacity.

Next steps / asks from HelioTech:
1) Confirm embedding payload pattern (single vs batched).
2) Share expected concurrent warm chat sessions (or a peak-day estimate).
3) Decision: prioritize tail latency vs cost? We can run a short bench (48 hours) on your staging to validate these numbers — would you like Redwood to run it?

We're happy to walk through the attached workbook in a 30–45 minute call and finalize a recommendation for procurement.

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
